newsitem.title: UK: GOLF-TURNER HOLDS ON TO LEAD BUT LANGER LOOKS OMINOUS.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-TURNER HOLDS ON TO LEAD BUT LANGER LOOKS OMINOUS.

text.p: New Zealander Greg Turner added a second round four under par 68 to his opening 67 to retain a one-stroke lead at the halfway stage of the Benson and Hedges International on Friday.

But Bernhard Langer of Germany, winner of last week's Italian Open, moved ominously into contention with a 66 which took him into a three-way tie for second on 136 with Briton Ross McFarlane, who also had a 66, and South African Retief Goosen (67).
Langer began with birdies on each of the first four holes, including a 60-foot putt on the par three second.
"I got off to a hot start," said the German whose only dropped shot among seven birdies was at the short 13th when he pushed a six iron shot into a bunker.
"My putting has been better than average and my shot-making is better as well," said Langer who has turned to the long handled putter after periodically suffering the 'yips' on the greens.

Turner, who like Langer played in the afternoon when the weather again turned nasty with sharp showers and squally winds, had looked to be heading for a second successive 67 until he dropped his only shot on the daunting 585-yard par five 17th.

"I hit a fairway bunker then went into the rough where the ball sat right down... I used discretion -- I need the money too much -- and decided to lay up instead of attempting to carry the water and then just chipped onto the green and two putted from 12 feet."
But a startling rainbow over the course as Turner putted out on the 18th may have signalled the 116,660 pounds ($189,000) could be coming his way.
Darren Clarke of Britain shared the lead with Turner for much of his round but dropped shots on each of the last two holes left him alone in fifth place.
At the 17th he drove into a bunker and took a six while at the 18th he needed three putts to get down from the front of the green.

McFarlane, who has yet to win a tournament since joining the European Tour 14 years ago, was delighted with his 66 and initially was celebrating setting a course record only to learn that at the same time Eduardo Romero of Argentina was completing a 65.
Romero's seven birdies and no dropped shots took him to a 138 and a share of sixth place with Britons Ian Woosnam and Lee Westwood and Patrik Sjoland of Sweden.
McFarlane's nine birdies were slightly offset by three bogies but the 35-year-old still rated it the best round of his career.

Colin Montgomerie, whose stated aim is to win a tournament in his first four weeks of rejoining the Tour, looks certain to have to wait a little longer after stumbling to a 71 for a halfway total of 141.
The challenge of veteran Irishman Christy O'Connor, second overnight just one behind Turner, also fell away as he struggled to a two over 74 and a two-round total of 142.
